title: security: under the PROTECTED profile, repository content (.moe/project.json settings.agentCommand) chooses the binary the agent wrapper runs on the host
description:
architect-4ae016fb flagged this in RF05 rev 2 (task-b439d7fb) as an unowned R01 gap: the R01 memory names it "agentCommand and WSL/native sessions under strong", nominally R10's, and no open row covers it. The human approved filing it as HIGH on 2026-10-30.

What the code does
- moe-jetbrains TerminalAgentLauncher.kt:267-268 resolves the command as `agentCommand ?: <project state>.settings.agentCommand ?: "claude"`. The project state comes from .moe/project.json, which is repository content. The value goes to the wrapper as --command / -Command (buildBashCommand, buildWslBashCommand, buildPowerShellCommand), with no check of RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile, so it applies under RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED too.
- scripts/moe-agent.sh (~360-440) parses --command into a binary and argv, then runs it. The basename only classifies codex, gemini or grok; anything else is treated as claude. There is no allowlist. Check the ps1 twin.

Why it is in scope
RF05's threat model puts repository content in scope, including ignored .moe files a pull can overwrite, and rules that a file under the project may add a refusal but never an admission. Choosing which binary runs on the host is an admission.

Required
Under PROTECTED, the agent binary a seat runs must not be selectable by repository content. The architect picks the mechanism, for example IDE-level user settings, or a fixed set of known agent CLIs resolved from trusted locations. Cover both wrappers. VS Code parity can be a follow-up row. Decide whether RF07 (task-f3f364a6) should dependsOn this row.
definitionOfDone: Under RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED, the JetBrains launch path never hands a repository-supplied agent command to the wrapper. A ./gradlew test case covers a project.json that names a non-standard command.

Under PROTECTED, moe-agent.sh and moe-agent.ps1 refuse to run an agent binary chosen by repository content, with a message naming the rejected command. Launcher tests cover it, and scripts/tests/parity-check.sh passes.
Legacy (non-protected) behavior is unchanged, or the change is documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md.

implementationPlan.description:
In moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/util/TerminalAgentLauncher.kt:

1. Add `internal sealed interface AgentCommandChoice { data class Run(val command: String); data class Refused(val message: String) }`. The known set is `AgentProvider.entries.filter { it != AgentProvider.CUSTOM }.map { it.command }` (~:144), so the menu's providers and the guard cannot drift apart.
2. Add `internal fun agentCommandFor(profile, explicit, projectSetting): AgentCommandChoice`.
   - LEGACY: return Run(explicit ?: projectSetting ?: "claude") exactly as today.
   - PROTECTED: candidate = (explicit ?: projectSetting)?.trim() ?: "claude".
     - Run(candidate) only when it is in the known set.
     - Otherwise Refused("Protected execution profile: the agent command '<value>' (<from .moe/project.json settings.agentCommand | custom command>) is not one of claude, codex, gemini, grok, so no agent was started. Pick an agent from the Agents menu.").
     - Truncate the value to 200 characters and replace control characters, matching the wrapper's MOE_PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMAND_REFUSED rule.
3. resolveContext (~:224) currently has `val resolvedCommand = agentCommand ?: MoeProjectService...settings?.agentCommand ?: "claude"`. Replace it:
   - the profile is PROTECTED exactly when `selected != null`; do not read project.json a second time;
   - call agentCommandFor(...);
   - on Refused, Messages.showErrorDialog(project, message, "Moe") and return null, so no terminal and no wrapper start;
   - on Run, use its command.

Change nothing else: the legacy branches, the CUSTOM menu flow, the stored custom command and buildCommand stay as they are. Under PROTECTED, a user-typed custom command is refused at launch with the same dialog, because the wrapper (task-aa85ff13) would refuse it anyway.

Error handling: the decision is pure and never throws. A null basePath is still handled by the existing early return. Run TerminalAgentLauncherTest until it is green.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN. TerminalAgentLauncher.kt (+35/-2): internal sealed interface AgentCommandChoice { Run(command), Refused(message) }; private PROTECTED_AGENT_COMMANDS = AgentProvider.entries minus CUSTOM, mapped to command (claude, codex, gemini, grok); internal agentCommandFor(profile, explicit, projectSetting): LEGACY -> Run(explicit ?: projectSetting ?: "claude") exactly as before; PROTECTED -> candidate = (explicit ?: projectSetting)?.trim() ?: "claude", Run only on exact case-sensitive membership, else Refused("Protected execution profile: the agent command '<shown>' (custom command | from .moe/project.json settings.agentCommand) is not one of claude, codex, gemini, grok, so no agent was started. Pick an agent from the Agents menu."), where shown = first 200 chars with Character.isISOControl chars replaced by '?'. resolveContext: profile = PROTECTED iff selected != null (no second project.json read); Refused -> Messages.showErrorDialog + return null, before AgentContext is built, so launchRole never creates a terminal or sends a wrapper command. Nothing else changed (CUSTOM flow, buildCommand, legacy branches). Verified under jetbrains-gradle lease (released): `cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.util.TerminalAgentLauncherTest"` -> BUILD SUCCESSFUL, exit 0; TEST-com.moe.util.TerminalAgentLauncherTest.xml tests=32 failures=0 errors=0 skipped=0. executionContract.intendedBehavior: Under RuntimeProfile.PROTECTED, the JetBrains launcher hands the wrapper only an exact known agent CLI name (claude, codex, gemini, grok). A non-standard value from .moe/project.json settings.agentCommand, or a custom command, is refused with a dialog naming it, and no terminal or wrapper starts. LEGACY is unchanged. docs/CONFIGURATION.md documents the IDE rule and the wrapper refusal from task-aa85ff13.
acceptanceCriteria: agentCommandFor rows: LEGACY passes values through, PROTECTED accepts exactly the four names, and every non-standard value is refused with the value named.
A temp project.json with executionProfile verified-local and agentCommand '/tmp/evil-agent' yields PROTECTED and Refused.
The combined gradle, protected-agent-command and parity-check command exits 0.
invariants: The known set derives from AgentProvider minus CUSTOM.
The refusal happens before any terminal or wrapper starts, and the message carries only the bounded, sanitized value.
compatibility: The LEGACY launch command is byte-for-byte unchanged, including custom commands and project.json values.
approvedScope: TerminalAgentLauncher.kt: AgentCommandChoice, agentCommandFor, and resolveContext's command resolution.
reuse: AgentProvider for the known set; the existing Messages.showErrorDialog refusal pattern in resolveContext.
sourceAssumptions: TerminalAgentLauncher.resolveContext (~:224-270): `selected` is non-null under PROTECTED; it resolves agentCommand from the explicit value, then project state settings, then "claude".
TerminalAgentLauncher.AgentProvider (~:144) enumerates CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI, GROK and CUSTOM.
RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile (~:57) maps executionProfile verified-local to PROTECTED.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A fixed set of known CLIs, matched by exact name (chosen; it is one of the task's suggested mechanisms). The set comes from the existing AgentProvider enum minus CUSTOM. The wrappers resolve the name from trusted PATH entries (task-aa85ff13).
- Ignoring project.json's agentCommand entirely under PROTECTED: rejected. The IDE settings dialog writes agentCommand into project.json, so honoring a known name keeps that working. A non-standard value refuses, which is fail-closed and visible, rather than silently falling back to claude.
- IDE-level storage of the command (PropertiesComponent): rejected, because workspace.xml can be committed too, and the CUSTOM flow already asks the user.
- One row covering both slices: rejected for size (6+ files, two harnesses). The wrapper files are also serialized behind CQ-R13c2 and many other wrapper rows, so the wrapper half is task-aa85ff13. This row keeps the JetBrains slice, the docs and the final verification, and it dependsOn aa85ff13 and 0c72d59a.
- RF07 dependsOn this row: yes. It is the CQ-RF integration task, so it must follow every CQ-RF row.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- TerminalAgentLauncher.resolveContext (~:224-270) selects the protected runtime: `selected` is non-null exactly under PROTECTED. It then resolves `agentCommand ?: state.settings.agentCommand ?: "claude"` and passes it as the wrapper's --command/-Command.
- AgentProvider (~:144): CLAUDE, CODEX, GEMINI and GROK carry their commands; CUSTOM is "".
- The panel's provider menu (MoeToolWindowPanel ~:205-221) passes provider.command, or the user-confirmed custom input, as an explicit command.
- RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile(basePath) (~:57) reads project.json strictly; verified-local maps to PROTECTED.
- MoeJson.parseProjectSettings is private, so the test reads agentCommand with Gson directly.
- docs/CONFIGURATION.md:179 holds the agentCommand row.
planningNotes.risks:
- This row starts only after task-aa85ff13, which waits on CQ-R13c2, and after task-0c72d59a. That ordering is intended.
- CONFIGURATION.md has many concurrent editors, so check its status before editing and never sweep a peer's hunks.
- A case-sensitive exact match is deliberate: it is the wrapper's rule, so the IDE and the wrapper agree.
- VS Code parity is not covered; it is noted for CQ-RF06.
